# Health, Safety and Emergencies
Colonial sites can be dangerous places. The Company takes your safety seriously, and these procedures exist to keep you alive. Please read them now, not during an emergency.
In any emergency, [bold]Corporate Security is in charge[/bold]. Do what they tell you, even if it contradicts this handbook.
## If the office comes under threat A threat could be armed intruders, a riot, wild animals or anything else that puts staff at risk. If you see or hear something that worries you, don't wait to be sure.
[bold]1. Get away.[/bold] If you can leave safely, do it. Leave your belongings and don't stop to look.
[bold]2. Lock yourself in.[/bold] If you can't get away, find a room with a door that locks. Lock it, stay away from doors and windows, keep quiet, and turn off anything that makes noise.
[bold]3. Call it in.[/bold] Once you're safe, report it on the Company radio channel. Say what you saw, where it was, and how many there were. Keep it short so the channel stays clear.
[bold]4. Wait.[/bold] Stay where you are until Security tells you it's safe. Don't open the door for anyone you can't identify.
Don't try to fight. Don't try to be a hero. Your safety is worth more to the Company than any equipment in the office.
## Lockdown Security may lock down the office. During a lockdown, stay where you are, keep doors shut and wait for further instructions. Don't try to override a locked door.
## Evacuation If the site is evacuated, Security will tell you where to go. Head straight there, help colleagues who need it, and stay with the group. Don't go back for your belongings.
The Company may send a shuttle to collect staff. Be at the landing area when you're told to be. The shuttle can't wait for anyone who's late.
## Injuries If you're hurt, get to the colony's medical staff as soon as it's safe to. If a colleague is hurt, stay with them if you can, call for help and tell Security where you are.
## Fire If you see a fire, get out of the room and close the door behind you. Report it straight away. Only use an extinguisher if the fire is small and you know how to use it.
## After an incident - Report what happened to the Liaison, in writing if you can. - Don't discuss the incident with anyone outside the Company. Refer any questions to the Liaison. - If you're struggling after a frightening event, please tell your line manager. You won't be judged for it.
